findings.summary: The per-flush axis is pinned at ONE point (the second forwarded commit), so a cost that begins at the FIRST or from the THIRD commit onward still survives -- both MEASURED green at 497/497. Do not fix in this commit.
findings.detail: Round 4's finding (`if (commits++ > 0) { currentLease(); currentLease(); }` surviving) is DEAD: re-measured, it now reds this test alone, 1 failure of 497. What remains is the residue of the same family, and both arms were measured on this tree with a `private int commits;` field added to RemoteSequencer and the mutation placed immediately after `Lease lease = currentLease();` in commitAll: (a) `if (commits++ == 0) { currentLease(); currentLease(); }` -- extra cost on the FIRST forwarded commit only -- SURVIVES, 497 tests / 0 failures; (b) `if (commits++ > 1) { currentLease(); currentLease(); }` -- extra cost from the THIRD forwarded commit onward, recurring forever -- SURVIVES, 497 tests / 0 failures. (b) is the worse of the two because it recurs per flush, which is the axis the SPEC cell calls PINNED. WHY IT IS ONLY MINOR, measured rather than asserted: every uniform per-commit and per-stream regression dies -- unconditional extra lease reads, a lease read per RunKey (gets 2 -> 5 at four streams), a per-stream PUT (puts 1 -> 4), a per-stream LIST (lists 0 -> 3), a per-stream STAT and a per-stream DELETE all red this test and only this test. The surviving family needs RemoteSequencer to grow a commit counter, and the class holds no mutable state at all by design. And the shipped tree is genuinely flat where the javadoc says it is: I probed the per-commit delta at commits 1, 2, 3 and 4, at one stream and at four, and every one is StoreCounts[puts=1, gets=2, lists=0, stats=1, deletes=0] -- so the javadoc's 'commits 1, 2 and 3 all measure (1, 2, 0, 1, 0)' is accurate and NOT an overstatement. The cheap strengthening, if it is ever wanted, is to widen the window over several consecutive commits and assert k x (1, 2, 0, 1, 0); it is not worth a sixth round here (review.md rule 11).
findings.failure_scenario: M5.6g rewrites commitAll to answer tryLead() from the lease the forwarder already read, and whoever writes it caches that lease on the RemoteSequencer instance with a refresh every Nth commit (N >= 3), or any later change adds a periodic re-read of period >= 3. The forwarded commit then costs 5 reads on one flush in every N instead of 3, per pod, forever -- and this test stays green, because it measures exactly one commit (the second) and the deltas it compares are both taken inside that one window. The SPEC cost row and the backlog cell both go on saying '+3 per follower commit, per-flush and PINNED'. MEASURED: `if (commits++ > 1) { currentLease(); currentLease(); }` after the lease read in commitAll leaves :sequencer:test at 497 tests / 0 failures, as does the `== 0` (first-commit) form.
